analysis.investment_thesis: AXISCADES scores poorly on both Magic Formula pillars: earnings yield of ~1.75% (EBIT INR 144 Cr / EV ~INR 8,243 Cr) is catastrophically below the 12% minimum, and ROIC of ~16% (EBIT/Invested Capital of ~INR 899 Cr) is mediocre rather than exceptional. The market is pricing in a decade of flawless execution for a company with a deeply erratic profit history.
key_strengths: Genuine revenue CAGR of ~12% over 9 years shows consistent top-line growth in defensible engineering services niches (aerospace, defense, ADAS)
OCF positive all 5 years (INR 61–122 Cr range) — business does generate real cash despite volatile net profits
High promoter holding at 58% aligns management skin-in-the-game
key_risks: Earnings yield ~1.75% — EV/EBIT of ~57x means you are paying a massive premium for modest earnings power
Chronic profit volatility: net losses in 2018, 2019, 2021, and 2023 — Magic Formula requires durable, predictable EBIT
Finance costs 37% CAGR over 9 years; borrowings exploded from INR 72 Cr (2022) to INR 346 Cr (2023), likely acquisition-driven leverage
red_flags: Earnings Yield of ~1.75% is one of the lowest possible scores under Magic Formula — stock is priced for perfection
4 out of last 9 years had net losses — this is not the durable earnings quality the formula requires
ROCE of 13.8% and ROE of 12.7% are below my 20%+ threshold for a 'good business' designation
Low FII (1.16%) and DII (1.63%) ownership signals weak institutional conviction at current prices
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula verdict is swift and harsh. Earnings Yield = EBIT INR 144 Cr / EV ~INR 8,243 Cr (Market Cap INR 8,037 Cr + Debt INR 258 Cr − Cash INR 52 Cr) = ~1.75%. That places AXISCADES in the bottom decile of any Magic Formula screen — I need to see north of 12% to get interested, and over 15% to get excited. The EV/EBITDA of 50.6x and P/E of 73x corroborate this: the stock is priced as if it were a high-growth software compounder, not a mid-size Indian engineering services firm.

The second leg, Return on Capital, offers only partial redemption. Using invested capital (Equity INR 693 Cr + Debt INR 258 Cr − Cash INR 52 Cr = INR 899 Cr), ROIC is ~16% — passable but not exceptional, and the company's reported ROCE of 13.8% is below my 20% bar. Worse, this ROIC is not reliably earned: net profits swung negative in four of the last nine years, including as recently as 2023. A business that loses money with regularity does not possess the durable competitive advantage that justifies a high return on capital premium. Both criteria failing simultaneously means AVOID — no amount of defense/drone narrative changes the math.
